Round 31 (#101 lesser P3, documented): `_PASS$` ended every case-insensitive pattern, so identifiers (`first_pass`, `compiler_pass`, `render_pass`) asked as if they were variable names. `_PASS` now names a secret only in capitals (`DB_PASS`); `grep -ri db_pass` still asks through the case-insensitive credential-name test.

Round 31 (#124, documented): `curl --form-string 'f=@.env'` sends the text `f=@.env`; --form-string never reads a file, so the block was an over-block. `-F`/`--form` file references (including each file of a comma list and every -F, not only the first) still block (g860-g862).

Round 31 (#79, documented): `find ~/.ssh -print` and `find . -name .env` print names only, as `ls` does; they were hard blocks only because the path operand is a secret store. A find whose -exec/-ok body or a downstream consumer receives the matches still blocks (g866, g867).

Round 31 (#79): `find . -name .env || true` is a standalone listing (names only), like g865; `||` routes no output. Any pipe, command or process substitution, coproc, -exec or -files0-from keeps the block (g884-g895).

Round 33 (#67, documented): an option whose value is a file the program CONSUMES prints nothing: `node|bun|deno --env-file=.env`, `docker run --env-file .env`, `dotenv -e .env`, `gcloud ... --key-file=...`, and an rsync/tar `--exclude=.env` pattern (text that keeps a file OUT of a copy). `vercel env pull .env.local` WRITES the file. The container/dotenv/node forms are exempt only when nothing on the line can print the consumer's environment: no command after the image, `dotenv -e X -- CMD` with a build tool, `node|bun|deno` running a script file (g1050-g1052, g1090-g1091: a pipe OUT of the consumer, or a pipe into a container run without -i, is not a stdin source; a stdin source into node/bun/deno, or into an interactive container, blocks: g1075-g1089); `env`, `printenv`, `sh -c`, an interpreter, `-e/-p/eval/data:` print it and block (g1030-g1049). The same files named as an operand of a program that prints them, `docker compose ... config`, and a consumed file beside a command that prints the variable still block (g992-g996). Where the output goes does not change this.
Round 33 (#67, documented): `git config KEY VALUE` SETS a value, so `core.sshCommand "ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy"` is text; `git config KEY` and `--file`/`--list`/`--get` forms still read and still block.

Round 33 (#67, documented): a GUI launcher (`code`, `subl`, `gedit`, `open -e`) hands the file to a window and prints nothing, so it is not a read when its output goes nowhere. Its output-routing wrappers (a pipe, a redirect, a substitution, a coproc) are NOT covered by this entry and keep the block (g1072-g1074). Terminal editors (vim, nvim, nano, emacs ...) stay readers, as on main (g989 and g1029 relabeled block), because the Bash tool has no terminal.

Round 34 (#188 function bodies, documented): `f() { stat .env; }; f` blocked on main only because `f()` was read as an unknown program that prints its operands; the function header is peeled and `stat` (metadata only) is judged, like the unwrapped `stat .env` (allow, g272).

Round 35 (#188): `time` before an assignment is not the command: `time VAR=/tmp/x; rm -rf $VAR` blocked on main only because the segment opened with `time`, so the assignment was not seen and `$VAR` was unknown. The assignment is read now (a provably safe path), the same decision as without `time` (allow). A value of `/` or `~` still blocks.

VAR=/tmp/x rm -rf $VAR`), or inside a heredoc or process-substitution body of its own, was hidden on main by the leading word or the missing body scope; it is read now and the decision equals the unwrapped row (allow). An assignment inside a subshell, group, branch, loop or function never proves a variable safe (it can only make one unsafe), so those forms keep their main decision.

Round 36 bare-word printer gate: main asked on `$(…)` wrappers of already-allow commands because `$()` tokenization fabricated a bare-credential operand (`$(rg token`, `$(git credentials`). The plain rows stay allow; head only soft-asks when the real program is a content printer / test runner / git-curl-sort context, so these wrapper false positives go allow.

Round 36c: Capitalized soft-ask carve-out is a tiny UI-verb allowlist (collect/confirm/approve), not a binary denylist. Cap interpreters/printers (Python3/Node/Paste/…) ask. Not an allowlist of those bypasses.

Round 37: `grep -L` and `ag -L` are --files-without-match(es): they print file names and never a line, so a secret-name search under -L cannot show a value (main already allowed the same search under -l, -c, -q and the long forms; the short -L was the one quiet mode not read). rg's -L is --follow and still asks (g1250). `--exclude` alone does not allow (g1251), a line-printing recursive search still asks (g1246-g1249).

Round 37: `-L` joined `-l`, `-c` and `-q` as a quiet mode, and a quiet grep/ag is not checked against its operands (the `continue` in ruleSecret), so a secret-store operand (`.env`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `credentials.json`) now allows under -L where main blocked it. Files-without-match prints names only, never a line, the same as -l/-c/-q, which main already allows on the same operands (g1260-g1262); the store's content is not read into the transcript. Line-printing forms and rg -L (--follow) still block (g1263-g1264).

Function-header fix (owner-reported false ask on `getSession() token`): main read a function-definition header (`name()`, `function name()`) as the PROGRAM and the bare word `token` as its operand, and read interpreter source (`node -e`, `python -c`, a stdin heredoc) line by line as shell, so a call line such as `getSession() // fetch token` asked. Now a header (any bare, unquoted name bash accepts: `a::b`, unicode, a leading digit) is peeled and its body is still analysed (the block controls g1293-g1305 keep blocking, and the subshell-body rows g1298 and g1306-g1309 now block where main allowed them), a first word that cannot be an executable name (parentheses, `;`, `=`, `//`, `#`; NOT braces, which brace-expand to a real program, and not a quoted word) is not a content printer, and the bare-word soft ask does not fire for it. Nothing here names a secret store: a store shape (`.env`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`) still blocks behind every such word (g1311-g1314), and a real reader after junk (`// cat token`) still asks (g1289, g1290). Every pre-existing corpus row (g1-g1265) keeps its decision.

closure.justification: Nesting past the documented `-c` cap: the plain row (3 shell wrappers) asks, and one more wrapper puts the payload beyond the 3 unwrap layers, which the guard documents as invisible (SKILL.md, README, `kit.test.mjs` 'round 4 documented limit'). Making the cap ask instead of allow is a design decision for the owner (tracked in #1); until then it is exempt.

`env` takes every leading word holding `=` as an assignment, a path included, so `env ./a=b token` sets a variable and runs the program `token` with no operand: allow is bash's reading. The plain row `./a=b token` asks because the shell itself runs `./a=b` with the operand `token`. Wrapped in env the pathed word is no longer the program (see mid-word-expansion.test.mjs). Filed under #103 (assignment-spelling words that the peel must treat like `A=b`).
